wj.d.L: Width $L$ of the infinite well (logarithmic slider)
wj.d.show: Draw the wave function $\psi_n$ or the probability density $|\psi_n|^2$ on each level
wj.d.ni: Level the electron starts in (or drag the knob at the tail of the arrow on the level ladder)
wj.d.nf: Level the electron moves to (or drag the knob at the arrowhead on the level ladder)
wj.goal.photon: A jump between two levels emits or absorbs one photon with $hf = \Delta E = E_\text{high} - E_\text{low}$, so $\lambda = hc/\Delta E$
wj.goal.width: The width of the well sets the colour: $\Delta E \propto 1/L^2$, so $\lambda \propto L^2$
wj.obs.n2: $E_n \propto n^2$: the gaps grow with $n$. At $L = 1$ nm, $2 \to 1$ gives 1099 nm (IR), $3 \to 2$ 659 nm (red), $4 \to 3$ 471 nm (blue)
wj.obs.L2: Halve the width and every wavelength becomes 4 times shorter; on the logarithmic strip all lines shift together by the same distance
wj.obs.region: At $L = 0.2$ nm, $E_1 = 9.40$ eV and $2 \to 1$ gives 44 nm (UV); near 2 nm the same jump is in the IR
wj.obs.abs: Swap $n_i$ and $n_f$ (or double-tap an end of the arrow): absorption needs a photon of the same wavelength, shown as a dark line on a continuous spectrum
wj.obs.nodes: State $n$ has $n - 1$ nodes; the states of a jump are drawn in front
wj.assume.electron: Particle: an electron ($m = m_e$) in a one-dimensional infinite well; levels from $E_n = n^2h^2/(8mL^2)$, the same values the Ch 39 solver gives
wj.assume.scale: Both axes follow $L$: the well always fills the panel and the energy axis runs to $27.5\,E_1$, so the picture looks the same for every width while the numbers change
wj.assume.pick: Drag the knobs (circles marked ▲▼) at the ends of the arrow up or down: they snap to the nearest level ($n \le 5$). Double tap either knob to reverse the transition
wj.assume.amp: Wave-function heights in arbitrary units (every state drawn the same height); the baseline sits at the state's energy
wj.assume.dipole: Every pair of levels is given a photon, as in the textbook problems (in reality some transitions hardly ever happen)
wj.assume.log: Spectrum strip: logarithmic wavelength axis from 5 nm to 5 µm; X-ray below 10 nm, visible band taken as 380 to 750 nm; lines outside the visible are grey and dashed. Clear button: removes the collected lines, keeping the current one
